blocks.x: A working build of Agentic AI & Hyperautomation for Life & Annuities: the operating context that shapes it, the services sequenced through the method, and the deltas we commit to.

Life books run on decades-long promises: underwriting quality at issue, servicing responsiveness across 30-year relationships, and actuarial integrity across regime changes (IFRS 17/LDTI). The machinery deciding those outcomes is data and document heavy — ideal ground for governed automation.

items: APS records, paramedical data and financial underwriting arrive as documents; assembly consumes days per case.
Surrender, loan and beneficiary transactions route through document-heavy queues with abandonment risk.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Intelligent Document Processing, Agentic Process Automation, Autonomous Workflow Orchestration from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Underwriting evidence assembly, Policy servicing transactions, Claims/beneficiary processing) on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — IFRS 17 / LDTI among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: See the work as it actually runs: event-log truth before you automate anything.
One automation spine: APIs, events, RPA and agents composable under common control.
Workflows that recover from failure on their own — long-running business processes that adapt, retry and recover without tickets.
APS/paramedical/financial docs classified, extracted and assembled (case cycle time down 40-60%)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: entity-link analytics scoring claims and applications against ring patterns (organized-fraud capture up 25%+). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
